text.p: An Irish Republican Army ceasefire in its 28-year-old guerrilla war against British rule of Northern Ireland took effect at midday (1100 GMT) on Sunday.
The IRA issued no fresh statement. Its decision to call a "complete cessation of all military operations" was announced in a statement on Saturday.

The truce, which restores an August 1994 ceasefire which the guerrrillas broke in February 1996, will allow its Sinn Fein political wing to take part in peace talks in six weeks if Britain judges the ceasefire to be genuine.

Hardline Unionists, who want the province to remain British, are threatening to walk out of the negotiations because Sinn Fein will be allowed to take part without the IRA surrendering any arms first.

But the province's biggest political party, the Ulster Unionist Party, has not made its next move clear pending talks on Monday between its leader, David Trimble, and British Prime Minister Tony Blair.
